description_full: Compañía de Minas Buenaventura S.A.A., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the exploration, development, construction, and operation of mines in Peru, the Americas, Europe, and Asia. It explores for gold, silver, copper, zinc, lead, and antimony deposits. The company also engages in the exploration, extraction, concentration, smelting, and marketing of polymetallic minerals and metals. In addition, it is involved in electricity transmission and generation; hydroelectric plant operation; and production of manganese sulfate monohydrate, as well as tailings dam management. The company was incorporated in 1953 and is based in Lima, Peru.

financial_summary: Buenaventura Mining Company Inc is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $7.1B market cap on $1.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +5.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at -2% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 11% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $148M in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.17× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 6.8×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.4%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 29% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
